subject.title: fix: accept valid MCP tool schemas without strict inputSchema.type check

question: May OpenClaw depend on the pinned MCP SDK’s non-public `cacheToolMetadata()` runtime method to preserve output-schema and task guards after relaxed `tools/list` validation?
rationale: The patch’s functional behavior is focused and proof-positive, but whether a private dependency method is an acceptable long-term tool-validation boundary is a maintainer-owned contract choice rather than a mechanical repair.

options.title: Accept the audited SDK seam
options.body: Merge with the existing pin and behavioral coverage, and treat MCP SDK upgrades as requiring verification that metadata caching still preserves output-schema and task guards.

options.title: Require a public dependency contract
options.body: Pause this PR until the MCP SDK exposes a supported metadata-cache path or OpenClaw can use an equivalent documented API without private access.

recommendation.title: Accept the audited SDK seam
recommendation.body: Merge with the existing pin and behavioral coverage, and treat MCP SDK upgrades as requiring verification that metadata caching still preserves output-schema and task guards.

likelyOwner.reason: They recently landed adjacent `tools/list` runtime behavior on the same bundled MCP catalog path.
